gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-belgrano: Belgrano is a serif with curves that stay open and clear. Bruno Ace above it draws its letters with a ruler-straight line of constant width, so the heading feels engineered while the text beneath feels bookish.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-biorhyme: Drawn with a ruler, nothing swelling. Bruno Ace holds one constant line while BioRhyme, a text serif, lets its curve ends stop like brush strokes lifted early, so the two feel mechanical and handmade at once.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-biorhyme-expanded: BioRhyme Expanded is a serif that reads wide and bookish, with gaps that break each word into single letters and an open e. Bruno Ace's outline is the stark opposite.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-biz-udmincho: Bruno Ace draws every stroke with a ruler-straight constant width. BIZ UDMincho, a classic serif with shallow terminal curls and wide gaps, gives that rigid line a traditional, bookish counterweight that makes each font look sharper.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-copse: Bruno Ace draws a single-weight line like a plotter pen, with counters that stay connected to the outside. And Copse, a text serif, lets visible daylight through every curved opening, so it does the quiet literary work.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-cutive: Distinctive monoline strokes run through Bruno Ace, while Cutive, a classic serif, spreads wide tracking across running text and opens a generous c. The difference is the whole point.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-david-libre: David Libre reads dignified and refined, its terminals hanging open as a text serif should. Bruno Ace takes the top spot with letters built from one width of stroke, a lingering, expressive display voice.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-enriqueta: Enriqueta is a text serif with chalk curves that stop well before closing, literary and dignified. But Bruno Ace is the showier one, making every curve as thick as a straight stem.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-fenix: Glass-tube lettering, hollow and constant. Bruno Ace is all expressive display, and Fenix, a serif whose curved strokes end before they turn inward, handles the classic editorial text beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gentium-plus: Gentium Plus, a serif, gives each c the wide mouth of a pitcher, which makes it feel classic and refined on the page. Bruno Ace's flat, unswelling curves above it make the paragraph feel quietly human.
